description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).
Random init; prints the public interface of the task object to learn vocab and format.
Random init; prints method signatures and 3 examples from a non-eval seed to learn the prompt format.
No LayerNorm. Attention shift register (14 chars) + one AND-gate MLP unit per hand-written lexicon pattern, uniform attention sums polarity at '='.
Same circuit as lex_shift14_flat, but phrases with no lexicon evidence default to negative instead of positive.
Broad hand-written lexicon plus a negation layer: attention finds a negator within 15 chars, MLP flips polarity; positive tie default.
lex_big_negflip15 with negative evidence weighted 2x, since reviews hedge praise more often than they hedge criticism.
lex_big_negw2 plus negators as direct negative evidence (-1), routed straight to SCORE so the flip gate cannot reverse them.
lex_big_negw2_negatorw1 with the direct negator evidence raised to -2, the same strength as a negative lexicon word.
Back to negator weight 1, with 95 net new negative patterns. Several were copied from printed dev errors, so its dev score (0.790) is inflated.
lex_negvocab2_negatorw1 with sentence-specific words removed; adds a clean dev score on dev[600:] and a check of the eval-set assumption.
lex_negvocab3_clean with negation reach widened from 15 to 25 characters, roughly five words instead of three.
lex_negvocab3_clean plus a latching attention head: after but/however/yet/though/although, evidence is boosted by +1 (NEG_REACH back to 15).
lex_negvocab3_contrast plus weak 0.4 priors on common review and function words, and a *less suffix rule, for phrases with no lexicon hit.
priors_weak04 with the prior strength doubled to 0.8.
priors_weak04 circuit with the lexicon cut by hand to the most common review words, to measure how much of the big lexicon matters.
core_lex_small with negative evidence weighted 3x instead of 2x.
core_lex_small with a negated negative worth 0 instead of +0.5, so 'not bad' is neutral.
core_flipneg0 with a negated positive worth -2 instead of -1, matching the strength of a negative word.
core_flippos2 with the zero-evidence default switched to negative, to test whether the tie rule still matters once priors exist.
core_flippos2 plus 0.15-strength function-word priors written from general knowledge of review language, to give zero-evidence phrases a vote.
core_flippos2 with the contrast boost set to 0, to test whether the latching attention head can be removed.
Refactor of core_boost0: latch head, contrast patterns and the unused flip gate removed; 15 heads and 3 gates instead of 16 and 6.
core_nolatch with 6-bit +/-1 character codes in place of 32-dim one-hots: d_model drops from 480 to 150 and AND gates read bit codes.
core_binary with head size 9, the minimum that fits the 9 scratch channels; d_model 135.
Full 1100-pattern lexicon on the simplified circuit: 6-bit char codes, d_model 135, no latch, negated negatives neutral, negated positives -2.
big_binary plus a broad new tier of general review vocabulary written from general knowledge, not from printed errors.
core_dh9 with the W_o output projection removed from attention: heads write in place, and predictions should not change.
core_no_wo plus two-word idioms where single words mislead, such as 'not only' and 'at best'.
core_no_wo (idioms dropped) plus weak negative prefix rules un*, dis* and mis*, to cover rare negative words without listing them.
core_prefix_neg plus more negative-leaning affixes: over*, non*, anti*, pseudo* and *ish.
core_affix_neg2 plus positive-leaning suffixes *ful, *ive and *ous as weak priors.
core_affix_neg2 with negated negatives left negative instead of dropped, so the NEV gate is no longer needed.
core_nev_stays with the flip disabled (negators still count as direct negative evidence), measuring what block 2 is worth.
core_nev_stays with a 12-character shift register instead of 14; patterns that no longer fit are dropped.
core_nev_stays with a 10-character shift register; patterns that do not fit are truncated to stems instead of dropped. d_model 99.
core_w10_trunc with an 8-character shift register: every pattern is at most a 7-character stem. d_model 81.
core_w8_trunc with a 6-character shift register: every pattern is at most a 5-character stem. d_model 63.
Shift register of 7 characters, between core_w8_trunc and core_w6_trunc: patterns are at most 6-character stems. d_model 72.
core_w8_trunc with negative words weighted 1.5x instead of 2x, now that morphology adds negative evidence on its own.
core_w8_trunc with positive and negative words weighted equally, testing whether the separate negative weight can go.
core_w8_negw1 with a negated positive worth -1 instead of -2, so every full-strength weight is +/-1.
core_w8_flip1 with weak priors at 0.25 instead of 0.4, relative to the unit word weights.
Full big_vocab4 lexicon with every core winner: no W_o, 8-char truncated stems, negative affix rules, +/-1 weights, ungated negatives.
big_w8_affix with negative words weighted 1.5x, because equal weights left the full lexicon biased towards positive.
big_w8_affix with negative words weighted 2x, bracketing the 1.5x result from above.
big_w8_negw15 with a 10-character shift register, checking the register length on the full lexicon. d_model 99.
big_w10_negw15 with a 12-character shift register, to see where the register length curve flattens. d_model 117.
big_w10_negw15 with direct negator evidence halved to 0.5, re-testing that weight at full lexicon size.
Refactor of big_w10_negw15: negative evidence writes straight to SCORE, removing the NEV channel and one gate. d_model 88, predictions should match.
